svg.title: Completed Offer Specification v1.2
svg.desc: Completed fictional Maya Chen Offer Specification for the Expansion-Ready Website System, including buyer, trigger, evidence state, obligation, boundaries, delivery stages, proof, pricing status, market evidence, and unresolved assumptions.
svg.text: PRODUCTIZE YOUR DEV SKILLS · WORKBOOK PP. 33–38
Expansion-Ready Website System · fictional Maya Chen / Harbor Mechanical case

g.text: SPECIFICATION FIELD
CURRENT DECISION / SOURCE
Offer name
Expansion-Ready Website System · v1.2 / September 2026 fictional case record
Qualified buyer
Established regional home-service company with a responsible owner or marketing lead
and a real transition trigger.
Buying trigger
Expansion, seasonal campaign, rebrand, vendor transition, or site constraints interfering
with the transition.
Evidence state
Directionally supported by public and direct buyer research plus one paid engagement.
Market breadth and price sensitivity remain provisional.
Controlled outcome
Launch-ready, measurable, client-operable marketing site meeting agreed architecture,
lead-capture, analytics, migration, QA, and handoff requirements.
Core paid obligation
Readiness/architecture, approved content structure, implementation, forms/CRM handoff,
analytics, migration, QA, deployment, documentation, and stabilization.
Primary exclusions
Customer portals, open-ended application work, custom CRM, paid-media management,
ongoing SEO, new brand identity, unreviewed financing integrations, guaranteed outcomes.
Uncertainty route
Technical review or paid discovery before a material unknown becomes an implementation obligation.
Delivery stages
Readiness & architecture → system setup → implementation → QA & launch → stabilization & handoff
Proof assets
Role-attributed real work, labeled demonstrations, migration/QA artifacts, technical verification.
Pricing status
Separate pricing-system decision. Commercial price remains provisional.
Market evidence
Generic “better website” language drew weak response. Migration/analytics continuity and
content readiness drew stronger questions. Portal requests confirmed an exclusion need.
Harbor made one paid commitment; that is real evidence, not proof that the market is validated.
Delivery evidence
Content-approval delay created a readiness gate, one decision owner, and schedule rule.
Financing variation created a technical-review / discovery routing rule.
NEXT EVIDENCE QUESTION
Does transition-trigger framing keep attracting qualified buyers, and how often do content-readiness and financing options affect the core route?
